## The usual way

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- Slides in one app, worksheets in another
- Copy the same words into a handout, a website, a packet
- Fix a typo in one place… and miss the other three
- Make a separate version for families and an answer key for you
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
::: {.callout-warning title="The result" icon=false}
Five copies of everything, slowly drifting apart. Hours every week spent formatting instead of teaching.
:::
:::
::::

::: notes
Ask the room: how many places does the same lesson live for you right now? Slides, a doc, a shared drive, an LMS page, a printed packet…
:::

## The Chalkline way: one file, many outputs

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="34%"}
::: {.callout-note title="You write" icon=false}
**One plain-text file** per deck or worksheet: words, pictures, and a few labels at the top (title, type, who it's for).
:::
:::
::: {.column width="66%"}
::: {.callout-tip title="Chalkline makes" icon=false}
- **Slides** to present, and a **slide PDF**
- A **web page** and a **printable PDF** of each worksheet
- A **unit packet**: every printable in one PDF, with a cover and contents
- A **year packet** with every unit
- A **student**, a **teacher** and a **family** website
:::
:::
::::

::: notes
Everything in this sample was made this way. Open any slide deck or worksheet file in VS Code to see how little is in it.
:::

## Every unit gets a home page

- The unit's **objectives** at the top
- Every slide deck and printable, with links to the PDFs
- A **Unit packet (PDF)** button: all the printables, ready to send to the copier
- Nothing to list by hand: add a file to the unit folder and it appears

::: {.small-note}
Try it: open **Unit 1: Ancient Greece** in the sidebar.
:::

## Packets build themselves

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="55%"}
- Every worksheet, handout and reference in a unit, **in order**
- A **cover** with the objectives and contents
- Page numbers running through the whole packet
- Slides, posters and tests stay out
- Add an **outside PDF** (a map, an official form) with one line
:::
::: {.column width="45%"}
::: {.callout-note title="Teacher version" icon=false}
The teacher build makes **teacher packets**: the same pages plus answer keys, with an orange **TEACHER EDITION** tab.
:::
:::
::::

::: notes
Packets are made fresh from the source files, not glued together, so they always match the latest worksheets.
:::

## Vocabulary support, built in

Tap or hover a word with a dotted line to see its card: picture, 中文 and a simple definition.

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- Ancient Athens was a {{< vocab "democracy" >}}.
- Rome built a huge {{< vocab "empire" >}}.
- An {{< vocab "aqueduct" >}} carried water to the city.
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
::: {.callout-tip title="One list, used everywhere" icon=false}
The words live in one spreadsheet. Slides, worksheets, the **vocab app** and Quizlet/Kahoot exports all read it. **English is the goal; 中文 is support**, and never appears in quizzes.
:::
:::
::::

::: notes
Try the pop-ups now. Then open "History vocab 词汇" in the sidebar: all 25 words from both units, searchable in English or Chinese.
:::

## Three websites from the same files

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="33%"}
::: {.callout-note title="Students" icon=false}
Slides, worksheets, vocab. No answer keys.
:::
:::
::: {.column width="33%"}
::: {.callout-warning title="Teachers" icon=false}
Everything, plus **answer keys**, **speaker notes** and teacher packets.
:::
:::
::: {.column width="33%"}
::: {.callout-tip title="Families" icon=false}
The objectives, the **vocab app** and only the slides you choose to share.
:::
:::
::::

One label decides who sees a file: `audience: [teacher, student, parent]`

## Classroom tools in every deck

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- A **timer** on any slide (press **T**)
- A **clock** in the corner (press **K**)
- **Speaker notes** in a second window (press **S**)
- **Tap-to-vote polls**: no devices, no accounts
:::

## It always looks like your school

- Colors, fonts and logos are set **once**, in `brand/`
- Slides, web pages, PDFs and the vocab app all follow
- Change the brand file and **everything** updates

::: {.small-note}
No more fixing fonts slide by slide.
:::

## Editing with an AI assistant

- The files are plain text, so tools like Claude can read and edit them
- `CLAUDE.md` tells the assistant the rules for this course
- While you work on one worksheet, only that file is rebuilt: quick to check
- When it's done: save, and rebuild that unit's packet

::: notes
Example request: "Add a 5-question exit ticket to the Rome republic deck, with Chinese glosses on the key words."
:::

## How this sample is organized

```text
course/units/01-ancient-greece/
  index.qmd                   the unit page: title, objectives
  city-states-slides.qmd      a slide deck
  athens-vs-sparta.qmd        a worksheet (web + PDF)
  images/                     pictures for this unit
vocab/data/vocab.csv          the 25 vocab words
brand/                        colors, fonts, logos
```

## Make your own unit

1. Copy a unit folder, for example `01-ancient-greece`, and rename it
2. In its `index.qmd`, change the title and objectives
3. Edit or replace the slides and worksheets, keeping a `type:` label on each
4. Add your words to `vocab/data/vocab.csv`
5. Double-click **Start Chalkline**: your unit is on the site
